Yes — without the `caption` package, the usual way is to redefine LaTeX’s internal caption formatting.

### Preamble solution
Add this to your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent\textbf{#1.} #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother
```

This makes table/figure captions left-aligned.

### Example
```latex
\documentclass{article}

\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \noindent\textbf{#1.} #2\par
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatother

\begin{document}

\begin{table}[h]
\caption{This caption will be left aligned.}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{ll}
A & B \\
1 & 2
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\end{document}
```

### Notes
- This affects **all captions** in the document, including figures.
- If you want it only for a single table, a manual workaround is to avoid `\caption` and write the caption text yourself above the table.

If you want, I can also show a version that left-aligns only table captions but leaves figure captions unchanged.
